title: fix(plugin-kanban): the board stops showing a card order it persists nowhere (objectui#8826)
body:
Fixes #8826

Ruled on the card as batch #141 item 3, letter **B**, maintainer 「同意」: the board stops claiming a capability it does not have. The fence the ruling asked this body to carry, verbatim: 「order persistence is not a capability of this board; a spec card would be its entry」.

## What changed

`KanbanImpl`'s `handleDragEnd`:

- **Same-column drop** — the branch no longer reorders local state. The card returns to its position. Nothing is persisted, so nothing is shown as persisted.
- **Cross-column move** — the membership change stays and is still persisted through `persistCardMove`. The landing index is still computed and still handed to `onCardMove`, where it is still discarded; what changed is that it is no longer *painted*. The branch appends to the target column instead of splicing at the slot the card was released over, so the board claims membership and says nothing about position.

No new prop, no new persistence path, no new authorable key — `Clause-②: no` holds, and this is a strict narrowing of a claim rather than a widening of any surface.

Two README bullets advertised in-column reordering as a feature. They now say what is true. Letter C was refused for formalising the false success; leaving it in the docs would have been letter C by the back door.

## ⚠️ One mechanism claim in the ruling was falsified — the file, not the mechanism

The ruling's execution note reads 「`ObjectKanban.tsx`: the same-column branch of `handleDragEnd` …」. Re-derived by symbol (`git grep -nw handleDragEnd`): **`ObjectKanban.tsx` has no `handleDragEnd`**. The drag handler and the optimistic reorder live in `KanbanImpl.tsx`; `ObjectKanban.tsx` owns `handleCardMove`, whose `_newIndex` parameter and `void _newIndex` discard are exactly where the ruling says they are and are **unchanged by this branch**. Everything the ruling asked for is done, one file over from where it says.

`KanbanImpl`'s mirror-sync timing (objectui#8534 / PR #8825) is untouched. The mirror itself stays — the cross-column optimistic write still needs it, which is now what defends it in that card's pin.

## The two pins — both legs, in one file

`packages/plugin-kanban/src/__tests__/sameColumnDropIsNotClaimed-8826.test.tsx`, on the recorder objectui#8826 was measured with (a module mock of `KanbanImpl` capturing the `columns` prop per render, plus a capture of the board's real `onDragEnd`):

- **LEG 1** — a same-column drop leaves DOM order equal to the DATA order, on **both** data ownerships, records no new `columns` snapshot and reaches no `update`.
- **LEG 2, the lit control** — a cross-column move still emits the new membership snapshot and still writes it, with an exact-body assertion (`update('task', 'a', { status: 'in_progress' })`). Without this leg, LEG 1 would read green on a board whose drag path was broken outright.

The fixture puts two cards in the source column and asks for their reverse order, so "did not move" is distinguishable from "nothing was driven".

## Reverse verification — two arms, mutation proven on disk, restore proven by hash

Run from the committed fix (`1f1ec56`); every arm restores with `git checkout HEAD --` under a trap with absolute paths, and each restore is verified by the blob hash plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, never by an exit code.

| arm | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| **same-column** | re-add the optimistic reorder this card removed | **exit 1 — 3 failed / 5 passed.** The failures are exactly LEG 1 (internal), LEG 1 (external) and the sibling control in `columnsReachDomSameCommit-8534`. **LEG 2 stayed green**, so the instrument distinguishes the defect from a dead board. |
| **cross-column** | splice at the drop index again | **exit 1 — 1 failed / 9 passed.** The single failure is the external-path assertion in `crossColumnLandingPosition-8826`; LEG 1 and everything else stayed green. |

`KanbanImpl.tsx` HEAD blob `5cd6f3b0eaf34acafa223271f8619b4de09366e1`; mutated blobs `7a93f0098ec53e68f839bf8fb4fc8823040b3575` and `3f9b95415364fc026770ba297b4c30a76f2c3dea`; restored blob reproduces the HEAD blob byte for byte on both arms, and the tree was verified clean afterwards. The mutation scripts assert their anchor is present exactly once before writing, so a no-op edit aborts instead of passing as a run.

## Verification

All run at `1f1ec56`, exit codes captured to files before being read, never through a pipe. Heavy runs serialized through the shared verify lock with `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=objectui-8826`, verdicts read from its printed `VERDICT command-exit` line.

| check | exit | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-kanban/` (repo ROOT) | 0 | 56 files / 358 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban type-check` | 0 | both legs — `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, the second being what covers the test files |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-kanban lint` | 0 | 0 errors; this diff contributes 0 of the package's 216 pre-existing warnings |
| `check:changeset-presence` | 0 | 1 changeset declared for 5 published source files across 2 packages |
| `check:doc-snippets` · `check:doc-examples` · `check:readme-exports` | 0 · 0 · 0 | these three read package READMEs, and all three first exited non-zero as PREREQUISITE NOT MET; re-run to a real 0 after the scoped build the gates name |
| `check:doc-types` · `check:doc-fences` · `check:doc-example-ids` | 0 | — |
| `check:control-bytes` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check:test-path-roots` · `check:unreferenced-sources` | 0 | — |
| `check:vi-mock-specifiers` · `-inherit` · `-override-shape` | 0 | run because this diff adds two `vi.mock` call sites |

A dependency-closure build (`--filter '@object-ui/plugin-kanban^...' build`) and the doc gates' own 35-task scoped build were both run to a real 0 first; the type-check and the three README/doc gates were failing only for want of them.

## Acceptance notes

- **Q3 was already answered, contrary to the brief.** The dispatch carried the card's question 3 as unmeasured. It was answered and merged on 2026-09-10 by PR #8975, whose characterization pin is in the tree. Re-derived rather than cited: that instrument was run on the pristine base at the start of this work and passed, so the reading stands — the cross-column landing position is lost on both ownerships. The fix surface is therefore the wider one, and this branch covers both halves.
- **What "appended" is, and is not.** The board cannot compute the target column's record-order position from the `columns` prop alone: each column's cards are a record-ordered subsequence, and nothing carries their global interleaving. Appending is therefore the only slot the board can offer without claiming to know where the round-trip will sort the card — it is not itself a promise that the card will stay last. On the ownership that re-renders, the prop-driven re-sync corrects it inside the same commit; on the external ownership, the card sits at the end of the target column until the parent reflows. What is removed is the claim that the user's drop slot was honoured. ⚠️ The #8975 fixture cannot distinguish "appended" from "record order" — its moved card is last in the record array either way — and its assertion now says so in place.
- **noted, not filed — `KanbanEnhanced.tsx` carries a byte-for-byte twin of the removed reorder.** Left alone deliberately: it has zero non-test importers, its registry key was retired by objectui#8257, and the package `exports` publishes only `.` and `./style.css`, so it is unreachable from outside this package. Dead code is not a fileable class. Successor: none — no open PR touches this package.
- **noted, not filed — the exported `useQuickAddReorder` hook keeps its own local-order state.** It is a published export with no in-repo consumer and is not on this board's drag path. Successor: none.
- **Deviation from the claimed file surface, declared.** The claim named `packages/plugin-kanban/src/`. This branch also touches `packages/plugin-kanban/README.md`, `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/README-KANBAN.md` and `.changeset/`. The changeset is mechanically required. The two README bullets are the docs half of this very behaviour change (AGENTS.md commandment #2), and each was a one-line claim of the exact capability the ruling removes; shipping them unchanged would leave the board advertising in-column reordering in print.
